title: Policy File (v1)
description: Validates internal/model.PolicyFile / model.PolicyRule exactly as read/checked by internal/policy.Validate and evaluated by internal/policy.Resolve, and exercised by configs/examples/policy.json and the policy embedded in configs/examples/config.json. This is a single document containing a global default plus an optional list of scoped rules — not one file per scope level.

version.description: Must equal internal/model.SchemaVersion; internal/policy.Validate rejects any other value.

default.description: Global fallback outcome, used when no rule matches (or when "rules" is absent).

rules.description: Optional scoped overrides (model.PolicyFile.Rules, json:"rules,omitempty"), evaluated by internal/policy.Resolve/specificity.

PolicyRule.description: model.PolicyRule. "mode" is required; source/system/role/assetSha256 are independently optional selectors — any combination (including none) is structurally valid.

source.description: Matches Observation.RootID exactly when present (internal/policy.specificity, weight 1 — lowest of the four selectors).

assetSha256.description: Matches Observation.SHA256 exactly when present (weight 8 — highest of the four selectors). internal/policy does not itself enforce a SHA-256 shape on this field, though by convention it is a full lowercase hex digest (see common.defs.schema.json#/$defs/Sha256Hex).

$comment: Precedence is a strict, additive specificity score, most specific wins: asset (assetSha256, +8) > role (+4) > system (+2) > source (+1); "default" is the global fallback used when zero rules match. A rule may combine multiple selectors (e.g. system+role together), in which case its score is the sum — internal/policy.Resolve always picks the single highest-scoring matching rule, so ties are only possible between rules with an identical selector combination, which internal/policy.Validate rejects: two rules with the exact same (source, system, role, assetSha256) tuple — including all-empty, i.e. more than one selector-less rule — fail validation as a "duplicate policy selector". Plain JSON Schema cannot express this whole-tuple uniqueness constraint (uniqueItems would also require "mode" to differ, which is not the rule Go enforces), so it is documented here rather than schema-enforced.
